title: Hold a tape measure pulled out along a board with one hand while the other marks the board at 300 mm
instruction: Pull the tape measure's case out along the board, well past the red 300 mm line, and hold it there with one hand; with the other take the pen and dab one mark on the board right beside the tape's 300 mm line, then lift the pen.
context: Carpenters, fitters and anyone doing home repairs mark lengths on boards with a tape measure before cutting. The tape's spring winds it straight back in as soon as the case is let go, so one hand holds the tape out along the board while the other makes the mark at the reading.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed pine board, 1.8 cm thick, from 25 to 33 cm forward and from 16 cm right of the centre line (its right end) to 39 cm left of it. (2) A tape measure: its steel hook caught over a steel nail at the board's right end, its yellow painted-steel tape 19 mm wide running along the board's near part (its middle 27 cm forward), and its dark ABS-plastic case (150 g, 7 cm long, 3 cm wide, 6 cm tall, with a yellow rubber grip ridge 1.6 cm wide, 4 cm long and 3.5 cm tall on its top, toward its back) lying on the board against the hook with the tape wound in. The case slides only along the tape's line, up to 47 cm out; its spring pulls it back with about 2 N wound in and 3.9 N fully out, and winds the tape back in as soon as the case is let go. The tape shows a short black line every centimetre, a longer one every 5 cm, and a red line across it at 300 mm. (3) A loose marker pen, 12 g, 9 cm tall: a felt tip under a blue polypropylene square barrel 1.6 cm across, standing in a plastic holder 20 cm forward and 4 cm right of the centre line. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. A mark: each time the pen's tip comes down within 1.5 mm of the board's top (after being at least 4 mm above it), it leaves a dot there. Measured: the tape was out at least 1 cm past the mark when the mark was made. Beside the tape: the mark on the board within 2.5 cm beyond the tape's far edge (the edge away from the arms). 1.0: a measured mark beside the tape within 4 mm of 300 mm from the board's right end, no other marks, and the pen's tip at least 4 mm off the board; 0.5: a measured mark beside the tape within 1 cm of 300 mm (with other marks, or the pen still down); 0.25: the tape pulled out to at least 310 mm at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the pen and the tape's case still.
reset_notes: Let the tape wind in with its case against the hook, put in a fresh unmarked board, and stand the pen in its holder.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the tape's case slides along the board on a sprung slider (the tape's spring), its hook fixed at the board's end; the tape is shown in 3 cm pieces the task file lays out as the case's mouth passes them. The pen's ink is dots the task file lays where its tip touches the board. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
